mutations.because: K-D9's only refusal is a duplicate t on one track's same clock. Disabling the check lets two stops at the exact same t on the same clock through, which K-D9 refuses.

K-D8 scopes the duplicate-t refusal PER CLOCK: two stops sharing a t on different clocks are independent axes and legal. Collapsing the per-clock seen-set to one set across all clocks makes a legal cross-clock duplicate look refused.

orderedKeys appends unnamed keys at the end, so dropping tracks from LAYER_KEY_ORDER does not make it disappear — it falls into the same tail bucket as any other unrecognised key, which a plain 'tracks appears in the output' assertion cannot tell apart from tracks sitting at its declared sixth position. Only a fixture with an unnamed key written before tracks in source order proves the position.
